session.notes: Fictional date, questions, transcript and scores; exclude from real progress analytics.

captures.content_text:
examiner: How are you today?
learner: I am fine, thank you.
examiner: Please narrate the story, beginning with: One day, a student went to a public library.
learner: One day, a student went to a public library. Most desks were empty, but bags were on the chairs. Some students leaves their bags there for hours. The student asked a librarian for help. A week later, the library introduced a rule against reserving seats for more than thirty minutes. When the student returned, several desks were available, so he could study there.
examiner: If you were the student in the last picture, what would you be thinking?
learner: I would be thinking that the new rule was useful because everyone had a better chance to find a seat. I would be happy to study there again.
examiner: Should public libraries introduce rules to prevent people from reserving empty seats?
learner: I think they should. Public libraries are shared spaces, so empty seats should be available to everyone. A clear rule would also make it easier for librarians to explain the system.
examiner: Do you think shared workspaces will become more common in the future?
learner: Yes, I think so. More people can work away from a traditional office. Shared workspaces give them a quiet place to work without renting their own office.
examiner: Should local governments spend more money on public facilities?
learner: Yes, because many people depend on libraries and community centers. However, local governments should first ask residents which facilities they need most, so that limited money is used effectively.
examiner: That is the end of the practice interview. Thank you.
